question: AMD Senior Software System Designer (about 5 years of experience), round 2 (in person, about 1.5 hours, covering OS, concurrency and coding): the candidate was asked to **implement an LRU cache**, with follow-up questions asked while coding. The same round covered mutex vs semaphore, CPU caches, and sorting an array of 0s and 1s.
lookingFor: Choosing data structures that give O(1) get and put.
Clean implementation of a hash map plus doubly linked list.
Link to CPU caches and eviction policies.
followUps: How would you make the cache thread-safe and reduce lock contention?
How would you add a TTL to entries?
What other eviction policies exist (LFU, FIFO, Clock) and when would you use them?
How is this related to CPU caches and their replacement policies?
How would you implement it using only the C++ standard library containers?
